[b]January 20, 2027: The Central Committee[/b]

As the various aspects of federalisation were debated, the second peoples congress determined that the First Council, being a temporary institution, would not truly serve the people as a true organ of governance, especially with its primary corpus, the princes rapidly disappearing. As such, the second people's congress would vote to dissolve the First Council in favour of a newly appointed Central Congressional Committee or in short The Central Committee or Centcom. The committee, consisting of Erjk Malben and 24 ministers of state would act as the enacting force of the congress, as well as the central bureaucratic organ of the state. The ceremonial head of the Centcom would be the President of the Union, Piter Drømm, who held power only on paper, but not practically. 

Upon the success of the vote, a clamour broke out in the congress as the remaining marginalised monarchist factions and traditionalist factions accused the congress of attempting to swing the country further leftward, and ignoring the right of self-determination. However, these were soon drowned out by cajoling cries from the upper balcony of various socialist and left leaning cadres that had gradually arrived over the days of the congress, vetted carefully by the national cadre of the CPNT. 

In the meantime, Erjk Malben, seeking approval for a project to quietly disenfranchise the monarchists during the congress, would meet with the heads of the various coalitions in the congress to discuss bringing in, heavier topics which would cause the most severe reactions, quietly laying out a trap for the congress to authorise the SCSI to act quickly to quiet the dissent of the monarchists through strategic blackmail and asset seizure.
